newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Weekly API report shows gasoline steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Weekly API report shows gasoline steady.

text.p: Tuesday's weekly status report from the American Petroleum Institute was broadly neutral, showing perhaps a slight weakening in the seasonally key gasoline market, analysts said.

The report showed total U.S. gasoline stocks down just 408,000 barrels at 194.179 million barrels in the week ended April 25. Output and imports also were slightly lower but still running at fairly high levels of 7.733 million barrels per day (bpd) and 376,000 bpd, respectively.
The "implied demand" for gasoline nationwide actually fell in the week to 8.167 million bpd from 8.409 million bpd.
Paolo Nery, senior energy analyst for Pace Consultants of Houston, said he was not greatly impressed by the 2.0 million-barrel decline in New York Harbor (PADD I) reformulated gasoline stocks.
"It's a seasonal phenomenon. People are trying to replenish their supply" as the summer driving season draws nearer.

The driving season, which has traditionally run from around February to May and pushed gasoline prices up over each of the previous five years, has coincided with record-low inventories this year. But gasoline futures prices since end-January are down about 10 cents at around 63 cents gallon.
Nationwide, gasoline stocks at the end of last week stood 9.7 million barrels below last year's levels, compared with an 8.9 million-barrel year-on-year shortfall the previous week.
"Stocks are extremely low and there's been no panic like there was in heating oil last fall," said Aaron Brady, an analyst at Energy Security Analysis in Washington D.C.

Among the principal factors for the market's calm are the "huge levels of imports -- higher than I'vee ever seen," with gasoline imports running at levels about twice the levels seen last year, said Brady.

Also, news that Tosco Corp will restart its 150,000 bpd Trainer, New Jersey refinery in mid-May, idled since February, 1996, is easing any worries about a shortfall in the northeast of the country. The very high levels of production seen in the northeast (PADD 1) during the very high maintenance period earlier this year in "refinery row" (PADD III) in the Gulf of Mexico plants also served as a reminder of the ability of refineries to quickly crank up production to meet demand.
The latest API report showed Gulf area gasoline stocks rising last week by 1.3 million barrels.

Hornsby & Co analyst Nizam Sharief said the rising market on Tuesday, when May gasoline futures moved up 1.02 cents to 63.36 cents a gallon, might be a factor of the high futures open interest for the May contract.
While crude and heating oil futures edged lower in after-hourse trading, gasolien futures remained steady.
Among other key stocks figures, crude stocks rose nationwide by 1.87 million barrels to 315 million barrels, running some 17.6 million barrels above last year's level.
East Coast and West Coast fell by 1.3 million and 1.5 million barrels, respectively, but that was offset by builds of 2.5 million and 1.4 million barrels in the MidWest and Gulf.
Imports were running steady at 7.9 million bpd.
June crude futures in New York rallied 53 cents to $20.44 a barrel at the close but were down at $20.34/36 in after-hours trading.

Distillate stocks fell last week by 1.4 million barrels to 94.8 million barrels. May heating oil futures were the strongest in Tuesday's market and rose 2.38 cents to 53.91 cents a gallon but were off at 58.50/75 cents in after hours.
